title: Water
hookLine: a glass on the nightstand, still by morning; the water disc, and a week of setting the table so the water can go still
tomorrow: next, a flame seen through a hole in a screen. why the screen?

lines: RAIN CAUGHT IN A CLEAN CLOTH.
cards: A glass of water left on the nightstand overnight. By morning it's perfectly still, and you can see straight through it to the wood. Bump the table and it's gone, all ripples.
So what changes when the disc turns to water? In the method, almost nothing, Buddhaghosa says. In the object, everything.
Fill a bowl to the brim with clear water: rain caught in a clean cloth before it touches the ground, or any water that isn't cloudy. Set it somewhere sheltered. And look.

teach.h: SAME STEPS AS THE EARTH DISC.
teach.b: The steps are the earth disc's steps. Don't study the water's color, or the bubbles, or the rim of the bowl.
Keep to the plain fact of water, and name it softly: water, water.

teach.h: A BOWL FIRST; THE SEA LATER.
teach.b: Buddhaghosa adds that someone who has practiced before might take it straight from a pond, a lake or the sea; a beginner starts with the bowl.
The clearer image, when it comes, he likens to a crystal fan set in the air, or a mirror made of crystal. Water teaches one thing earth doesn't: stillness you can see.
The bowl only shows a clear image when nothing jostles it.
And this whole week lines up behind that bowl. The subject that fits you. A friend who chooses.
The snag cleared. The place that's good enough.
Each one is a way of steadying the table so the water can go still.

how: Where kasina practice is taught, the water kasina follows the earth kasina's method with a bowl of clear water set in a sheltered place; a teacher may suggest one kasina at a time.

o: a bowl of clear, still water used as a meditation object
a ritual washing done before every meditation session
a blessing sprinkled over a room before sitting

games.q: a friend wants to try the water disc with a glass of soda, because the bubbles are "more interesting." what would Buddhaghosa say?
o: use plain, clear water, and don't attend to color or bubbles.
fine; any liquid works, as long as you stare at it hard.
skip the glass and go to the ocean; bigger water works better.
games.why: the point is stillness you can see: clear water, sheltered, no color to study. the sea is for those who've practiced before.

practice: Set a glass or bowl of water where nothing will bump it, and look at the water itself, not the glass, naming it softly: water. When the sit ends, take one slow sip and taste how plain it is.

wordCard.voice: Water: the second kasina, a bowl of clear, still water used as the object of meditation.

orig.note: Pali: water (apo). The water kasina is the second of the ten.

carryVoice: Pocket this one: clear water, still enough to see straight through. A week of the forty, behind you.

sources.ref: Visuddhimagga V.3–4 (the water kasina: one with past practice may see it in a pond, lake or sea; a beginner fills a bowl with rain caught in a clean cloth or other clear water, sets it in a screened place, does not attend to color; the counterpart sign like a crystal fan or crystal mirror)
